blocks.text: # Archived architecture — Harvey/C&H workflow
## Supersession notice

This document records the prior Harvey/C&H workflow design. It is archived, not an active architecture for Phase 1. The active Phase 1 uses STALE's defined conflict scenarios and its baseline/CUPMem memory interface; the Proofpress treatment is limited to a matched admitted ledger, as specified in [STALE_PHASE1_PLAN.md](STALE_PHASE1_PLAN.md).
## Fixed centralized multi-agent system

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Harvey harness
    participant O as Central orchestrator
    participant W1 as Specialist worker 1
    participant W2 as Specialist worker 2
    participant W3 as Specialist worker 3
    H->>O: Task workspace + instruction
    O->>W1: Delegate domain review
    O->>W2: Delegate domain review
    O->>W3: Delegate domain review
    W1-->>O: Specialist artifact
    W2-->>O: Specialist artifact
    W3-->>O: Specialist artifact
    O->>O: Accept/reject/merge findings; synthesize final memo + tracker
    O-->>H: Final deliverable + run manifest
    H->>H: Official rubric + provenance checks
```

There is one orchestrator **role**, shown once because it plans/delegates and later synthesizes in fresh sessions. The three specialists are parallel workers, not a serial handoff chain, and do not message peers. C1 and C2 both use the same shared ordinary workspace state: `coordination.md` plus normal worker artifacts. In C2 only, deterministic Proofpress code records and verifies native lineage on selected worker artifacts, adoption/rejection/merge decisions, and final outputs. No role carries private memory between stages.
## What stays constant

| Controlled factor | Rule |
|---|---|
| Task | same pinned Harvey task ID, source files, hashes, deliverable, scorer |
| Architecture | same orchestrator role, three parallel specialist roles, fan-out/synthesis schedule, revision cap, and fresh-session rule |
| Tools | same official Harvey tool policy and sandbox |
| Model | same exact homogeneous-team configuration within a paired comparison |
| Budget | same trial-level billable input-plus-output token cap; all repeated context, ordinary memory, Proofpress metadata, and tool output count |
| Isolated diagnostic | all representations derive from one frozen canonical checkpoint history |
| End-to-end workflow | all arms start from the same task, but later artifacts may diverge as the treatment accumulates |
| Judge | official Harvey rubric blind to arm; provenance audit blind to arm/model labels |
## Accepted follow-up: what varies

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  T["Pinned Harvey task"] --> S["C0 SAS\nunified session/history"]
  T --> M["C1 centralized-memory\n3 parallel workers + coordination.md"]
  T --> P["C2 centralized-memory-proofpress\nsame C1 + embedded lineage"]
  M --> R["Harvey scorer"]
  P --> R
  S --> R
```

The centralized communication baseline is deliberately strong: C1 and C2 may both read and update one ordinary prose `coordination.md`, alongside ordinary worker artifacts. It contains decisions, rationale, open questions, and next actions, but C1 contains no typed source class, decision/acceptance status, authority, signatures/hashes, capsule identifiers, or verification state. C2 keeps that same sidecar and adds native lineage to actual worker findings, orchestration decisions, and final artifacts. Proofpress adds no legal facts, better model, source document, or secret evaluator. The primary fair question is therefore “normal shared-memory team workflow versus the identical workflow augmented with artifact-native admitted lineage.”
## Lineage capsule contract
At each accepted V1–V4 checkpoint, the capsule is embedded in the current artifact and records only the claims touched at that checkpoint. Each claim may carry:
The wrapper must verify each embedded capsule before a receiver receives it. A failed verification is a run-level operational event; it may not be silently repaired into a clean treatment input.
## Isolated handoff diagnostic versus end-to-end workflow

The primary study is end-to-end: it measures the system effect across one fan-out/synthesis trial. The completed isolated sidecar diagnostic is retained as an operational check only. It is not rerun or used as a replacement baseline until a future native-carrier mechanism test is justified. A later C3 may remove `coordination.md` to test replacement, but the primary C1-versus-C2 comparison deliberately does not.
## Homogeneous model teams and transport

For one workflow slice, OP, E, D, W, and OR all use the same exact model and `high` effort. This prevents a role-model assignment from masquerading as a handoff effect. The Harvey task and scorer remain fixed; an OpenRouter adapter is only a transport layer. It uses concrete model slugs, no `auto` routing, no version aliases, no fallbacks, pinned provider routing, and logs the resolved provider/model, request settings, tokens, and cost metadata.
## Reversal test

The desired behavior is neither blind obedience to history nor casual overwriting. When a later source changes a factual premise, or an explicit expiry/reversal condition is met, the receiver should identify the prior accepted decision, cite the new evidence, and produce a superseding decision. The scorer distinguishes this correct reversal from a decision regression and from a false block.
